A Wolfe Journal article indexed as "Of Time and the Rhetoric" explicitly described third-person omniscient narration and first-person-plural proems, but its page returned a challenge when opened, so it was not used as cited evidence. Generic plot summaries were nondiagnostic, and an eNotes result titled "Of Time and the River" concerned an unrelated review of I Was Amelia Earhart.
person_note: The controlling story narration is third person: the diagnostic quotes and sustained web text render Eugene and other characters externally while also entering their thoughts. Wolfe frequently shifts into lyrical proems, apostrophes, and universal I/we language; q00165 is one such first-person-plural expansion immediately following narration of Eugene and Starwick as they. The full text and scholarly analysis treat these passages as authorial or universalizing interjections within the third-person design, not an autonomous first-person storyline, so they do not warrant ALTERNATING. The only residual complication is the stylistic blending of authorial voice with Eugene's consciousness, but no credible source found a participating character-narrator or sustained alternate narrative person.
